_comment: Interface typedefs, single source of truth. tools/gen-interfaces.py
generates the SystemVerilog packed-struct typedefs and the matching C++
accessor header from this file.
WHY GENERATED. Stage 1a finding F-12: a packed-struct port surfaces in the
Verilated C++ model as ONE packed signal -- VL_OUT64(&iss, 38, 0) -- which
is exactly what the convention's §2 wants, but the FIELD OFFSETS are not
exposed. The C++ swap harness has to know the layout independently. A field
reordered in RTL and not in C++ gives a harness reading the wrong bits,
which presents as a functional bug rather than as a mismatch. That is the
drift §9 of the strategy doc names for parameters, arriving at the one
boundary §1's block-swap mechanism depends on.
WHAT IS AND IS NOT DECIDED HERE. The MECHANISM is Stage 1d. The interface
LIST is Stage 2's, and depends on the partition list, which §2 of the
strategy doc is explicit has not been decided. `issue_t` below is the
convention doc's own worked example, carried as a reference so the
generator, the checker pattern and the lint rules have something real to
exercise. It is marked provisional and is not a proposed interface.
FIELD ORDER IS DECLARATION ORDER, and in a packed struct the FIRST field
declared occupies the MOST significant bits. The generator computes offsets
from that rule and emits them for both languages, so nobody has to.
DIRECTION is recorded per interface (open item: direction discipline
without modports). Packed structs carry no direction enforcement, so this
at least makes the intent generated rather than remembered.

interfaces.name: issue_t
interfaces.doc: REFERENCE EXAMPLE, from the interface convention §2. Not a proposed interface -- the real list follows from the Stage 2 partition.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: Transaction valid this cycle. Control, so it carries an X-safety obligation.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Data. X propagates here; §6 prohibits X on control, not on data.

fields.name: tag
fields.doc: In-flight transaction tag. Control: it selects, so an X reaches a decision.
